title: Rahul's 136 and Gill's 98 put India 118 ahead at 486 for four in Wellington
dek: Rahul became the first Indian opener with Test hundreds in all four SENA countries. Rishabh Pant was unbeaten on 55 at the close of day three.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
KL Rahul made 136 and Shubman Gill fell two short of a century as India piled up 486 for four on the third day of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Saturday, taking a first-innings lead of 118 with two days to play.

Rishabh Pant was unbeaten on 55 at stumps, with the nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj yet to score, after Gill was bowled by Jacob Duffy three balls before the close for 98 off 146 balls. India lost only three wickets in the day on a dry pitch that gave the New Zealand bowlers little help.

## The day's play

India resumed on 159 for one, with Rahul on 52. He and Devdutt Padikkal added 165 for the second wicket in 55 overs; India were 239 for one at lunch and 277 for one at tea, according to reports. Rahul reached his 13th Test hundred soon after lunch, off 207 balls, making him the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), according to reports.

Padikkal, on 80 off 175 balls and looking set for his first Test century, was bowled by Kyle Jamieson after New Zealand took the second new ball. Rahul and Gill then added 91 before Nathan Smith dismissed Rahul, who hit nine fours and two sixes. Rahul had survived an appeal for leg-before on 5 on Friday: the umpire Kumar Dharmasena gave him not out, New Zealand did not review, and replays suggested the ball would have hit the stumps, according to reports.

Gill and Pant took the attack to the tired bowlers in the final session, adding 100, with Pant hitting several sixes over deep square leg, mostly off Duffy. Gill hit nine fours and two sixes.

Duffy finished the day with one for 180 from 29 overs, the fourth most expensive figures by a New Zealand bowler in Test history, according to reports. Jamieson, with one for 57, was the pick of the attack. New Zealand did not create a chance in one two-hour session, one report said.

## Earlier in the match

New Zealand, put in after India won the toss, recovered from 70 for five thanks to a 216-run sixth-wicket stand between Henry Nicholls, who carried his bat for 175, and Glenn Phillips, who made 118, and were all out for 368 on Friday. Jasprit Bumrah took four for 92 and Akash Deep three for 53. Yashasvi Jaiswal made 85 at the top of India's reply.

## What's at stake

This is the first of two Tests, with the second in Christchurch next week, and the series counts towards the World Test Championship, in which New Zealand lead the table and India are fourth. India will look to extend the lead quickly on Sunday morning and give Bumrah and the other bowlers as long as possible to bowl New Zealand out a second time.

Play on day four begins at 3.30 am IST on Sunday.
